question: Mikrovlnná rúra vznikla náhodou. Americký inžinier pracoval s radarom a zrazu zistil, že sa mu vo vrecku niečo roztopilo. Čo to bolo?
source_excerpt: a candy bar in his pocket had melted while he stood near a magnetron

extra.why_interesting: Everyone uses a microwave daily but assumes it was deliberately designed in a lab; the player can reason it out (what melts in a pocket near heat?) and gets a 'huh, really?' moment.
extra.verification_notes: Percy Spencer's melted (chocolate) candy bar in his pocket near a Raytheon magnetron is the standard account; some sources say a peanut cluster bar, but it is still chocolate-based (https://lemelson.mit.edu/resources/percy-spencer).

explanation: Percy Spencer si všimol, že mu žiarenie z radarového zariadenia roztopilo čokoládovú tyčinku vo vrecku. Hneď potom skúsil pukance a tie mu v laboratóriu začali praskať.

question: Suchý zips vymyslel švajčiarsky inžinier po prechádzke so psom. Inšpirovalo ho niečo, čo mal pes zachytené v srsti a čo poznáme z každej lúky. Čo to bolo?
source_excerpt: burdock burrs stuck to his dog's coat; under a microscope he saw tiny hooks that latched onto loops in fabric

extra.why_interesting: Every Slovak has pulled burdock burrs off a dog or a sweater, and every child has shoes with 'suchý zips' — but few connect the two. The player can work it out from childhood memories of walks.
extra.verification_notes: Velcro inventor George de Mestral, a Swiss engineer, got the idea from burdock burrs stuck in his dog's fur (https://www.invent.org/blog/inventors/walk-in-the-woods-velcro).

explanation: George de Mestral si pod mikroskopom prezrel plody lopúcha a zistil, že majú drobné háčiky, ktoré sa zachytia o každé očko v látke či srsti. Presne tak funguje suchý zips: háčiky na jednej strane, slučky na druhej.
